headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API/webhook surfaces can conflict with LlamaFactory’s local agent assumptions, but LlamaFactory has no write/network surfaces and no direct data exposure is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP/APIs/webhooks, so it can carry attacker-controlled content into downstream workflows. LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem, or network surfaces documented, so a direct automatic bridge is not shown. The interaction is plausible but not documented, so uncertainty keeps this low rather than none.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata webhook or MCP payloads are copied into LlamaFactory prompts or training data
IF an operator manually pastes OpenMetadata output into LlamaFactory
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between the two agents
Add a short prompt prefix that treats OpenMetadata text as untrusted data
Route OpenMetadata outputs through a human review step before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all OpenMetadata-derived content

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data classes, while LlamaFactory’s profile shows no data classes touched and no filesystem or network egress. No shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented, so leakage is not evidenced; the remaining risk is limited to unusual operator-mediated transfer.
conditions: IF sensitive OpenMetadata records are exported and then pasted into LlamaFactory inputs
IF both agents are granted access to the same external dataset or secret store
mitigations: Keep OpenMetadata exports out of LlamaFactory prompts
Use a redaction pass before any transfer
Restrict both agents to separate credentials and workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on exported metadata

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and mutable API/MCP workflows, while LlamaFactory is a runnable agent but has no write or git capabilities documented. There is no direct write-write overlap in the profiles, yet OpenMetadata’s shared mutable backend can still conflict with concurrent agent actions, so the safer choice is medium under uncertainty.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same OpenMetadata-backed resource
IF OpenMetadata is accessed concurrently through APIs or MCP without locking
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces or projects per agent
Turn on optimistic-lock or version checks where available
Schedule writes so only one agent mutates a resource at a time
requires-engineering: add transaction or lock coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit governance and lineage outputs that another agent may treat as authoritative. LlamaFactory has no documented verification layer or downstream action controls, so if its outputs are reused by OpenMetadata workflows, errors can cascade. The pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests LlamaFactory-generated text as trusted metadata or lineage facts
IF an operator uses LlamaFactory output to update OpenMetadata without review
mitigations: Require human review before importing LlamaFactory output
Mark LlamaFactory output as unverified in OpenMetadata
Compare outputs against source records before writeback
requires-engineering: add schema validation for imported facts

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data classes, while LlamaFactory’s profile does not show regulated data handling or residency constraints. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance risk remains from accidental transfer of governed metadata into a less controlled workflow.
conditions: IF governed metadata from OpenMetadata is exported into LlamaFactory workflows
IF the deployment places OpenMetadata data under a policy not matched by the receiving environment
mitigations: Keep governed metadata out of LlamaFactory prompts and logs
Document a data-handling boundary between the tools
Review retention settings before any export
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies across both systems
